part.text:
Done. Here's what I changed.

## Root cause

In `Context.res` (`src/context.ts:414`), the merge logic did:

```ts
const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
_res.headers.delete('set-cookie')   // ← wiped the incoming response's own cookies
for (const cookie of cookies) {
  _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
}
```

When assigning a new `Response`, it deleted the new response's `Set-Cookie` headers and re-added only the existing response's cookies, so the handler's cookie was lost. (Also note `Headers.entries()` yields `set-cookie` once per cookie, so this block ran repeatedly.)

## Fix — `src/context.ts:414-433`

Read the existing cookies once, skip `set-cookie` while copying the other headers, then append the existing cookies to the new response's headers without deleting the incoming ones:

```ts
const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
for (const [k, v] of this.#res.headers.entries()) {
  if (k === 'content-type' || k === 'set-cookie') {
    continue
  }
  _res.headers.set(k, v)
}
for (const cookie of cookies) {
  _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
}
```

Now both the middleware cookie and the handler response's cookie survive.

## Tests — `src/context.test.ts`

- Updated the existing re-assign test (which had encoded the buggy behavior) to expect `cookies.length + newCookies.length` with both sets present.
- Added a regression test at `src/context.test.ts:448` that models middleware setting a cookie on `c.res`, then a handler returning a `Response` with its own `Set-Cookie`, asserting both cookies are retained.

## Verification

```
pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  64 passed (64)
```

All changes are unstaged, left for your review.
